meta.Site / zone: Sanjay Lake Park, East Delhi (DDA) - pathway works area

headlineFindings: This is an active works area inside the park green boundary. Construction material covers about 6% of the frame on average and peaks near 12%, and the site-wide construction flag is raised in roughly 83% of analysed frames.
Broken brick and stone rubble is the largest single component, in several discrete piles left directly on and beside the walking track rather than in a contained compound.
Aggregate and cement stockpiles plus stacked slabs sit on open ground with no hoarding, sheeting or barrier visible anywhere in the clip.
The walking track is obstructed - material spills onto the running surface, and the Infrastructure score carries the obstruction penalty through much of the clip.
Cleanliness is the worst score on the site at around 20/100, driven by the combination of construction material and pre-existing loose ground debris at roughly 28% of open ground.
Ground is heavily disturbed: bare and excavated earth averages about 24% of frame and peaks above 40%.
No safety signage, barricading or worker PPE could be resolved at this altitude - absence of a detection is not evidence of absence on the ground.

recommendations.Finding: An active works area is operating inside the park green boundary with construction material spread across open ground and no hoarding, sheeting or barricading visible anywhere in the clip.
recommendations.Recommended action: Confirm the works are sanctioned. Require the contractor to hoard and sign the site, contain all material in a defined compound, and produce a site-safety plan before works continue.

recommendations.Finding: Material is spilling onto the walking track, obstructing the pedestrian route through the park.
recommendations.Recommended action: Clear the running surface immediately and provide a signed, barricaded pedestrian diversion for the duration of the works.

recommendations.Finding: Broken brick and stone rubble is left in several piles on open ground; aggregate and stacked slabs are stored unprotected. Combined material cover averages about 6% of frame and peaks near 12%.
recommendations.Recommended action: Remove or consolidate rubble into a contained compound; sheet stockpiles to prevent wash-off, particularly given the proximity of the lake.

recommendations.Finding: The lake edge is within the same frame as the works. Uncontained fines and rubble are a direct wash-off risk into the water body, which is already eutrophic elsewhere in the park.
recommendations.Recommended action: Install silt fencing between the works and the bank; prevent any site material or washings entering the lake.

recommendations.Finding: Bare and excavated ground averages around 24% of frame and peaks above 40%; the surface is churned by site traffic.
recommendations.Recommended action: Programme full reinstatement - decompact, regrade and re-establish ground cover once works complete. Hold retention against reinstatement.

recommendations.Finding: Loose ground debris sits at about 28% of open ground on top of the construction material.
recommendations.Recommended action: Daily housekeeping on the works area; sweep the adjoining path.

recommendations.Finding: Material and site traffic are encroaching on tree root zones and shrub margins.
recommendations.Recommended action: Install tree-protection fencing to the root protection area; keep material off planted margins.

recommendations.Finding: This clip is exactly the case the framework's geo-tagged work-verification proposal targets.
recommendations.Recommended action: Supply the sanctioned works schedule and the park boundary polygon so this zone can be checked against approved scope and fed into contractor scorecards.

recommendations.Finding: Barricading, signage and worker PPE cannot be resolved from 4K nadir imagery at this altitude.
recommendations.Recommended action: Add a low-altitude pass (15-25 m) over active works areas, or pair drone survey with a ground safety audit.
